newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: YPF, partners to invest $265 mln in Bolivia.
newsitem.headline: YPF, partners to invest $265 mln in Bolivia.

text.p: Three Argentine oil companies -- YPF SA, Perez Companc SA and Pluspetrol SA -- signed contracts to commit a total of $265 million in capital to their joint Bolivian subsidiary, Empresa Petrolera Andina, YPF said on Thursday.
The $265 million investment over three years will go toward boosting Andina's production of crude oil and natural gas, YPF said in a letter to the Buenos Aires Stock Exchange.
YPF said the actual investment by Andina will probably exceed that amount.

The three Argentine companies took control of Andina in the privatization of Yacimientos Petroliferos Bolivianos late last year. Andina currently produces 10,000 barrels of oil and three million cubic meters of natural gas a day.

Andina is 50 percent-owned by a joint venture made up 40.5 percent by YPF, 40.5 percent by Perez Companc and 19 percent by Pluspetrol. The other 50 percent is held by Bolivian private pension funds. YPF is the operating partner.
YPF said it hoped Andina's growing gas production would eventually contribute to a gas pipeline from Bolivia to Brazil.
